title: verify_chain crashes on the documented default path with no dispositions argument

finding.claim: verify_chain crashes on the documented default path with no dispositions argument
finding.evidence: The function documents that omitting the disposition store preserves legacy behavior, but later unconditionally returns a variable that is only assigned inside the dispositions-present branch. Calling verify_chain with its default 'dispositions=None' will raise UnboundLocalError instead of returning a result.
finding.recommendation: Initialize 'chain_consumed' before the conditional, or only reference it inside the same 'if dispositions is not None' branch where it is created. Add a test that calls verify_chain without a dispositions argument and asserts it returns normally.

probe.summary: Chain probe (`probes/closing_disputes_probe.py`, section d): verify_chain was called with dispositions=None at HEAD — it returns the full verdict dict (hold_active=True; the chain's deterministically-derivable fields computed) WITHOUT raising. The None handling the claim says is missing is present: core.py:4674 initialises `chain_consumed = [e for e in dispositions or [] if ...]`, and None is defaulted before any use. The recorded refutation's own concession ('chain_consumed can be None on some path') is not borne out at HEAD — every path defaults it.
